title: The rejected error returns as a distractor
statement: Have the worked example reject a likely error aloud, then offer that same error as a wrong option in the independent check, attempted cold with no hint first.
detail: A Grade 3 course's lesson structure has the guide weigh three candidate sentences in the worked example and reject two aloud, and in the independent turn one wrong option of the first four-option check is the exact error the guide rejected. A Grade 5 audit upheld the same design when it was challenged as spoiling the independent item: the canonical design pins the rejected alternative to the worked example, the trap item is attempted first with no hints before the try, and its repair appears only in feedback after the attempt.
against: The challenge it answered held that the modelled rejection pre-teaches the trap item's repair, so the independent item draws nothing out; it was refuted by appeal to the canonical design and the cold attempt, not with learner data (`grade3-reading/artifacts/u4l2-build/GRADE5-DECISION-LOG.md`, lines 184-191).

evidence.quote: Step 1 = 4-option check on what to hunt (one distractor = the exact error Scout rejected in I-do)

canon itself pins the rejected hunter-to-prey alternative to the M2 I-do (G5-BAR §10: T-U4L2-01 is "carried by the I-do at M2, with the rejected hunter-to-prey alternative") — pre-modeling is the canonical design, and the release re-elicits it cold.
